stem: Which of the following graphical representations is most appropriate for depicting the time-series data of a company's monthly sales revenue over 24 consecutive months?

options.text: Bar chart with separate bars for each month

per_option_rationale.rationale: A line graph best shows the trend, continuity, and movement of data measured at successive time points. It makes the pattern over 24 months immediately visible.
A pie chart shows parts of a whole at a single point in time (proportions). It cannot represent change over time across 24 periods.
A histogram is for continuous quantitative data in classes (frequency distribution), not for time-series data where the x-axis represents ordered time periods.
While a bar chart can show data for different months, 24 separate bars do not emphasize trend or continuity as well as a line graph does; a line graph is the standard choice for time-series data.

explanation: Time-series data has a natural temporal order where trend and continuity matter. A line graph (also called a time-series graph) plots values against time and connects points with lines, making trend visible. This is the standard ICAI-recommended representation for time-series data.

explanation_sections.punchline: Time-series data over consecutive periods is best depicted by a line graph to show trend and continuity.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: match data type to appropriate graphical representation. Decision tree: is data continuous over time? Yes - use line graph. Is data showing parts of a whole? Use pie chart. Is data a frequency distribution with classes? Use histogram. Are data discrete categories? Use bar chart. Monthly sales revenue over 24 months = time-series = line graph.
explanation_sections.lesson: The decisive match is: time-series = line graph; frequency distribution = histogram; parts of whole = pie chart; discrete categories = bar chart.
explanation_sections.timing: 20 seconds. Identify data type: time-series. Match to graph type: line graph. Trap: option 3 (histogram) is for frequency distributions of continuous data, not time-series.
